feature: One commander row — the play-style sentence, the mechanic gap, one Fit
note: Written at close-out. Four cells: both lanes at both widths, because the row is ONE component serving two populations and the whole ruling (D1) is that nothing on it may be read off ownership — so a sheet showing only one lane would photograph the ruling's easy half. `/discover` is where the price draws and `/commanders` is where it never does: every commander there is owned, and §7.4 row 5 unmounts the slot. The three gap-slot occupants cannot be forced by a step, so the sheet shows whichever the fixture's top rows carry; `unplayed` and `allPlayed` both appear on this account, and `noMechanics` is 3.5% of the catalogue and may not. What the sheet CANNOT show is the states matrix — that is `commander-row.test.tsx`'s job, 28 cases — nor the two browser-measured figures, which are `probe:commander-row`'s. A picture proves the row rendered on the route; it does not prove a state.

shares.why: The point of the feature. Two routes, one row, and `check:shared` is what proves they converged rather than each growing a copy — which is exactly what `rec-card.tsx` and `discovery-row.tsx` were before this round.
